video_title: Trae Young breaks silence: Hawks exit, Wizards, doubters, family & becoming NBA villain| The Pivot

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his commitment to the Atlanta Hawks
quotes.excerpt: I wouldn't trade any moment that I've had in the NBA back for anything.
quotes.quote: I wouldn't trade any moment that I've had in the NBA back for anything. Being in Atlanta was unbelievable. It's crazy how eight years just went like this.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young believes he is entering his prime
quotes.excerpt: I haven't played very much in a year and a half, I'm probably just entering my prime.
quotes.quote: I haven't played very much in a year and a half, I'm probably just entering my prime. I know if we start winning, imagine the Wizards as the number one team in the East next year. What people going to be saying? That's what changes the narrative.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young reflects on playing through injury in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: What I know now, I would have played through my sprained ankle.
quotes.quote: What I know now, I would have played through my sprained ankle. We were two games away to go into the finals. You never know when that opportunity is going to come again.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his background and handling criticism
quotes.excerpt: I can't get caught up in what people are saying now as mad as it makes me.
quotes.quote: I can't get caught up in what people are saying now as mad as it makes me and what people say about me is not true. We all go through stuff, man. I know it may seem like Oklahoma is soft.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on the 'Next Steph' narrative
quotes.excerpt: For me, going into college, I was definitely not like a goal of mine.
quotes.quote: For me, going into college, I was definitely not like a goal of mine or something I'm thinking about, but that's when that gets brought up. It's like, what are you going to do? Be like, no, I'm not like in. For me, I was just focused on my game.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on why he attracts hate from opposing fans
quotes.excerpt: I think that hate gets drawn the way it does because I look in the crowd and I see a lot of people look just like me.
quotes.quote: I think that hate gets drawn the way it does because I look in the crowd and I see a lot of people look just like me. I got cousins, I have white side or black side, I got a lot of people that I look in the crowd and that look just like me. Same height, everything, and they saying these things to me, but I know it doesn't come from real hate, I think it comes from just a little bit of jealousy.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his connection to Texas Tech and his father
quotes.excerpt: I was born in Lubbock, my dad played at Tech.
quotes.quote: I was born in Lubbock, my dad played at Tech. And so when I went to play at Tech, I didn't expect that. I remember that was the morning, the morning of shoot around that morning, the Cavs played the Thunder and LeBron. Someone asked LeBron about me going to the draft and stuff and he was talking about he doesn't have to think about if he's going to come back to school or not and blah, blah, blah. And it just got blown up and I remember feeling so excited.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his persona as a villain
quotes.excerpt: I'm not a villain outside of the court.
quotes.quote: You embrace it to an extent when you're on the court, you know what I'm saying? But if someone wants to get with it or get like an interaction out of me and try to be a villain outside of this, it's like I'm not a villain outside of the court, you know what I'm saying? And that's what I hope you get from me.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his favorite crowd-silencing moment
quotes.excerpt: I told everybody that it's quiet in here.
quotes.quote: I told everybody that it's quiet in here. I hit a floater to hit the game winner and that was my first ever playoff game. So for me to hit the game winner after like that that chance starting from 10 minutes from the first quarter on, it was crazy.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his relationship with Spike Lee
quotes.excerpt: Spike is as much as everybody says so many things, he's been such a good person to me and my family.
quotes.quote: Spike is as much as everybody says so many things, he's been such a good person to me and my family. He's giving me one of his books, I mean, has a handwritten letter in it that he wrote and gave it to me, I think it was after that series or at the end of that and I mean, just been nice to my pops and everything. So he's just been a great dude and that's the head of New York, you know what I'm saying?

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his relationship with his younger brother
quotes.excerpt: I always wanted a big brother.
quotes.quote: I always wanted a big brother. Being the oldest of my family, having two younger sisters before Timothy, I always just you always envision yourself like having an older brother that you can lean on, like if something you're going through something or things aren't easy. A lot of people think that like how I grew up was just easy, being here in Oklahoma, but it just wasn't.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his competitive drive and chasing greatness
quotes.excerpt: I was chasing the greats. I wasn't even chasing my pops. I was chasing the greats.
quotes.quote: I was chasing the greats. I wasn't even chasing my pops. I was chasing the greats. I was chasing Steve Nash, I was chasing Chris Paul and I mean Chauncey Billups. I mean, everybody like I was chasing the ones that were winning championships at the time, Tony Parker. I was getting those types of in visions. I already seen myself past my pops.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his draft night experience
quotes.excerpt: I was nervous. I thought I was going to Orlando at six.
quotes.quote: I put in all caps, I put relax. Be like, relax, you going to be all right. You going to be all right. So I was I was nervous. I thought I was going to Orlando at six. I had worked out for New York, they were at nine, they were talking about trading up with Fizdale and I worked out with the Bulls at seven and I did work out with the Hawks they were at three, but I didn't really know if I was going to go that high.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his trade to the Atlanta Hawks
quotes.excerpt: I knew at the fourth pick right after the third pick when Luka got traded, I was told my agent.
quotes.quote: I knew at the fourth pick right after the third pick when Luka got traded, I was told my agent tapped me and said, he's not going there, you're going there. So I knew during their whole little five minute wait period in the fourth pick and then there was another five minute wait period. So I knew I was getting drafted at five.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his academic and athletic balance
quotes.excerpt: I felt like I could have been top five in my class.
quotes.quote: I felt like I could have been top five in my class. I should have been top 10, number one point guard I felt like, but I was number four. So was I slept on a little bit maybe, but this is I mean, it's starting to feel a certain way.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on the importance of community facilities
quotes.excerpt: There can never be enough courts in the world in my opinion.
quotes.quote: There can never be enough courts in the world in my opinion. And because there's there's too many people. Like there's too many people and not enough courts. So we can always have more courts built in in areas and places and that just allows people and certain communities that can't necessarily spend this money to go to this this facility, they can spend it to come to this one that's maybe a less a little less expensive.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his approach to taking tough shots
quotes.excerpt: I think the only time it's really a bad shot is when it's for certain guys.
quotes.quote: I think the only time it's really a bad shot is when it's for certain guys is like that level of shooting like when it's early in the shot clock off like and when there's no momentum on your side. Like there's no momentum on your side and you just come down and you take a bad shot or you just take a quick three. Like that may be considered a bad shot unless it goes in. Every coach will tell you that.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on balancing fatherhood and his NBA career
quotes.excerpt: When I had him, I started being I started being afraid to fly.
quotes.quote: When I had him, I started being I started being afraid to fly. So I started being afraid to fly and I was and I play in the NBA, like we fly every day. So it's like, how am I going to play if I can't fly? You know what I'm saying? But it was just more about the fact that I I didn't want to not be here for my kids. And so my my dad, I mean, like I said, he's me and him, I don't butt heads with nobody else more on this world than my dad, but some of the best advice I've ever gotten from in this world is from my dad.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his faith and finding peace
quotes.excerpt: I've always been a believer in God and I've always grown up. I'm not perfect by any means.
quotes.quote: I've always been a believer in God and I've always grown up. I'm not perfect by any means, but I mean, I've always been that way. And being in the NBA, you're you're so busy, you're traveling and there was a point where I didn't want to go to church because I feel like there's so many eyes on me and I can't be myself like I was when I was 12, 13, 14 in a church. And so I stopped going to church for a while and and then he told me to to just get back into it, like in into the Bible.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on the emotional toll of his college team's struggles
quotes.excerpt: I'm crying. There's times that I don't think I'm ever going to play for the university
quotes.quote: I'm crying. There's times that I don't think I'm ever going to play for the university that I grew up going to and watching their games and stuff. It's all just because the ACT that I took my freshman year. If somebody would have said something about it my junior year of high school, I probably would have redid it, but they wanted to bring it up right before my freshman year of college.

quotes.speaker: Channing Crowder
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Crowder and Trae Young discuss the Knicks-Hawks playoff matchup
quotes.excerpt: What do you think it's going to take for either of those teams to win this championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Crowder
text_blocks.text: You look at the league right now and the way that it's transitioning. Obviously, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, two-time MVP, gets beat by Victor Wembanyama and the Knicks. They run through the East. When you look at that matchup from a hooper's standpoint, what do you think it's going to take for either of those teams to win this championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Trae Young
text_blocks.text: It's going to be a battle. I think it's a battle of two different types of beasts. Obviously, you got San Antonio with the alien, and Wembanyama is one-of-one, man. He has a chance to be special and something nobody's ever seen. I pray that he stays healthy just for the game itself. You want to see somebody like him just play.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young credits Spurs trainer Tim Martin for his development
quotes.excerpt: People need to show a lot more love to Tim Martin, who's sitting behind their bench.
quotes.quote: People need to show a lot more love to Tim Martin, who's sitting behind their bench. This is his first year with them, with the Spurs. He's been Wembanyama's trainer since he's been like 13, 14. He used to train me, and I remember going down and working out with him in Christmas and him being like, 'I got to go over here to Paris and work out this 7-foot 15-year-old. He's going to be special, watch.' And he ended up being Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his preference for playing with smaller guards
quotes.excerpt: I've always pulled for the smaller guards. I always like the underdog.
quotes.quote: For me, I've always pulled for the smaller guards. I always like the underdog. As much as New York may hate me and say 'fuck you Trae' after the game, that's fine. I wish they played us on Christmas. I'd spoil their Christmas every year. I promise you.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Clark
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Clark asks Trae Young about Jalen Brunson's leadership in playoffs
quotes.excerpt: What we've seen from Jalen Brunson throughout these playoffs, really putting this team on his back.

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: As great as you are, the heights you reached in Atlanta, what we've seen from Jalen Brunson throughout these playoffs, really putting this team on his back when people didn't even think he could be the lead dog on a championship-caliber team. Would Jalen Brunson finding a way to lead the Knicks to the championship show that a smaller guard who is ball-dominant can lead a team to a championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Trae Young
text_blocks.text: Yeah, for sure. I can play multiple ways. A lot of people just see what I've done and me being ball-dominant. I can't wait to show other things. My boy Dejounte Murray, who's with me 24/7, he was my point guard for a lot of years and I was just a shooter. I didn't do nothing but just shoot the ball. So I can't wait to show that. But also, yes, you can win with a smaller guard, of course. It's been done before.
